blocks.content: Calderas are the most explosive of the earth's volcanoes and tend to collapse on themselves rather than building any tall structure.

items: The Deccan Traps of India are a classic example of a Flood Basalt Province, frequently tested in UPSC Preliminary and Mains exams.
Shield volcanoes are non-explosive under normal conditions but become explosive if water enters the central vent.
Questions often contrast basaltic lava (low viscosity, fluid) of shield volcanoes with andesitic lava (high viscosity, explosive) of composite volcanoes.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Shield volcanoes are predominantly composed of fluid basalt lava, creating broad, low-sloped structures.
Composite volcanoes erupt cooler, highly viscous lava along with pyroclastic debris, building tall, layered cones.
Calderas are extremely explosive volcanic depressions that collapse inward post-eruption rather than building elevated cones.
Flood Basalt Provinces release vast quantities of highly fluid lava covering thousands of square kilometers, exemplified by the Deccan Traps.
Mid-Ocean Ridge Volcanoes occur along oceanic spreading ridges extending over a global network of oceanic basins.
